item.title: Your Portfolio vs. Tariffs: Which Sectors Survive 18-20%?
item.description:
J.P. Morgan projects U.S. effective tariff rates hitting 18-20% by mid-2026. Marcus and James break down which sectors get crushed first — construction, autos, apparel — and which ones quietly win. Plus: the counterintuitive case that tariffs might actually help manufacturing long-term, and what that means for your 401k right now.

Morgan Global Research, March 18, 2026 — U.S. effective tariff rates approaching 18-20% by mid- • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, CNBC, March 4, 2026 — Section 122 tariff raised from 10% to 15%; t • Reshoring Initiative 2025 survey — 500+ manufacturers: 15% additional tariffs on all imports encoura
Next episode: If tariffs reshape manufacturing, which domestic industrials are actually positioned to capture that — and which are just riding the hype?

item.title: Your 401k This Week: Why the Fed's Tariff Silence Is Actually Bullish
item.description:
The Fed hasn't called an emergency. Hasn't cut rates out of cycle. Hasn't even flinched. This week Marcus and James debate whether that silence is the most bullish signal of 2026 — or just the calm before a very bad storm. Yale's Budget Lab puts tariff costs at $800 per household. J.P. Morgan sees the effective tariff rate hitting 18-20% by mid-2026. What does any of this mean for your 401k right now?
